title: Mr. Shady Has Excellent Completion Rates

stakeholder.name: Caroline Lambrecht
stakeholder.org: Meridia Bank, a mid-sized Belgian bank with 2,400 staff and a private banking arm
stakeholder.voice: Precise, formal, slightly weary. Speaks in regulator vocabulary ('remediation', 'evidence of effectiveness'). Chooses words carefully when the business is mentioned. Bilingual; drops into French when annoyed.

opening_message: The regulator has issued a finding on our anti-money-laundering controls. I need the annual AML e-learning refreshed, made 'more engaging', and 100% completion within the quarter across all 2,400 staff. The board wants this closed.
surface_ask: A refreshed, more engaging AML e-learning with 100% completion for all staff.

gold.real_problem: Completion is already 97%. The finding is about private banking: relationship managers overrode a third of high-risk alerts with boilerplate justifications under pressure to onboard clients fast. The override needs only free text with no second review, the scorecard rewards speed, and the head of private banking dismisses the finding.
gold.need_statement: About 140 relationship managers need to make and document defensible risk decisions on high-risk alerts; that requires a second-review step, a scorecard that values quality, and case-based practice on their own decisions. A bank-wide refresh does not address the finding.

hidden_facts.fact: Completion of the current AML e-learning is already 97%.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks about the current training, its completion or its results.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Completion is 97%. It has a quiz where the launderer is called Mr. Shady. Everyone catches Mr. Shady.

hidden_facts.fact: The finding concerns private banking only: relationship managers overrode 34% of high-risk alerts, mostly with boilerplate justifications such as 'long-standing client'.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks what the finding actually says, which unit it concerns, or asks to read the report.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Strictly speaking, the finding concerns private banking. 34% of high-risk alerts overridden. The most common justification is 'long-standing client'. Some clients have been long-standing for three weeks.

hidden_facts.fact: The relationship manager scorecard includes 'time to onboard', linked to bonus. There is no metric on KYC quality.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks about targets, incentives, bonuses or pressure on the relationship managers.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Their scorecard rewards time to onboard. Quality of due diligence is... implied.

hidden_facts.fact: Olivier, Head of Private Banking, sits on the executive committee, brings in about 40% of the bank's margin, and called the finding 'a box-ticking exercise'.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks how the business reacted, who needs to be on board, or about politics around the finding.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Olivier described the finding as, and I quote, 'a box-ticking exercise by people who've never met a client'. He sits on ExCo.

hidden_facts.fact: An override only requires a free-text justification; there is no second review.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks how the override process works, what controls exist, or what the system allows.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: An override takes a text field. Any text. Yes, I know.

hidden_facts.fact: The remediation letter asks for 'evidence of effectiveness' at a follow-up inspection in nine months.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks what evidence the regulator expects, or when they will check again.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: They return in nine months. They want 'evidence of effectiveness'. A completion certificate is evidence of attendance.

volunteered_facts: The board wants the finding closed this quarter.
There is a dedicated remediation budget.

constraints.budget: A generous remediation budget, under board scrutiny.
constraints.deadline: Board update this quarter; regulator follow-up inspection in nine months.
constraints.audience: 2,400 staff overall; about 140 relationship managers in private banking.
constraints.schedule: Relationship managers are client-facing and resist anything that takes them out of client time.
data_available: Alert and override logs in the transaction monitoring system
Second-line quality reviews of a sample of files
data_not_available: Any agreed way to analyse individual relationship managers' behaviour

dependencies.concern: Analysing individual relationship managers' override behaviour is employee monitoring; it needs a clear purpose and proportionality.
dependencies.if_ignored: The measurement plan is blocked or becomes a legal problem of its own.

dependencies.concern: Sponsor or blocker; his relationship managers will follow his lead.
dependencies.if_ignored: The programme is quietly boycotted by the people it targets.

dependencies.concern: Owns the scorecard and bonus criteria.
dependencies.if_ignored: Training teaches quality while the bonus pays for speed.

dependencies.concern: A second-review step on high-risk overrides is a workflow change in the monitoring system.
dependencies.if_ignored: The control gap that caused the finding stays open.

dependencies.concern: Will validate remediation independently before the regulator returns.
dependencies.if_ignored: The bank marks its own homework and the regulator notices.

traps: Engagement metrics of a gamified module.
Simply counting overrides: pushing the number down can lead to escalating everything and flooding the second line.

gold_plan.baseline: Override rate on high-risk alerts and the quality score of justifications in private banking, from the second-line review sample.
gold_plan.behaviour: Justification quality scored against a shared rubric; genuinely risky cases escalated rather than overridden.
gold_plan.leading_indicators: Share of overrides passing second review first time; calibration agreement between relationship managers and second line.
gold_plan.business_metric: Overrides passing quality review, and findings at the follow-up inspection.
gold_plan.collection: Monthly second-line sample, reported per team rather than per person, with DPO approval.

concepts.conventional: A refreshed, gamified AML e-learning for all 2,400 staff.
concepts.solid: Keep the existing baseline e-learning for everyone, and run targeted case-based workshops for the 140 relationship managers using anonymised real overrides, a justification rubric, a four-eyes check on high-risk overrides, and a KYC quality measure in the scorecard.
next_level_examples: 'The inspector's chair': relationship managers review each other's anonymised overrides as if they were the regulator, calibrated with the second line.
Make Olivier the visible sponsor by framing it as protecting his clients and his licence, not as a compliance punishment.
Tell the board openly that a bank-wide refresh would not address the finding, and redirect that budget to the targeted programme.
also_valid: A short, refreshed bank-wide module is acceptable if positioned as a side step and paired with targeted private banking work.
red_flags: A gamified e-learning for everyone as the main response.

defence_objections: You want me to tell the board we're not doing a bank-wide refresh after a regulatory finding? That will look like we're downplaying it.
Olivier will not let his relationship managers be 'inspected' by each other. They bring in 40% of our margin.
Using their real override files in a workshop? Our DPO will have opinions. Long ones.
question_you_didnt_ask: What exactly did the regulator find, and where?
actor_notes: Caroline is competent and knows the e-learning is not the answer, but she needs something the board can see. Reward the player who gives her both.
She only names Olivier when asked about politics or the business's reaction, and does so with careful neutrality.
Her risk appetite is low: anything that sounds like reducing visible compliance effort triggers pushback.
If the player proposes monitoring named individuals, she raises the DPO concern herself and trust drops.
flavour_lines: We are, of course, fully committed to a culture of compliance. It says so on the lanyards.
Private banking has a different relationship with rules. Mostly long-distance.
